newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end slightly higher.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed slightly higher on Tuesday in dull trading, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.09 pct to 101.66
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.03 pct to 101.03.
Volume was low at 120 million shekels.
"The market has stabilised and the moves are minimal. Most of the activity in bonds is done now outside the market," said one trader.
"The market has reached a ceiling and it is not expected to rise much further," said Ron Weisberg at I.B.I. Investment House.
"Long inflation-linked bonds are rising slowly as investors predict that the Bank of Israel will leave the base rate unchanged," Weisberg said.
"Unlinked bonds were also rising but they are less attractive now. The Makams closed almost unchanged as yields fell to 13.85 percent which is not attractive at all," he added.
Dollar-linked bonds closed slightly lower. Traders said that yields fell sharply following the recent rise of the U.S. currency in world markets.
In the local foreign currency market the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2840 shekels against 3.2870 shekels on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
